description: Table 7 is a single tabular image (no plots, micrographs or schematics) listing X-ray line-profile parameters for the ferrite (110) reflection in two Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels. Columns are: Peaks | Aging states | 0.02Nb (Θ, β, βcosθ, 4sinθ) | 0.04Nb (Θ, β, βcosθ, 4sinθ); no units are printed for any column. Only one peak, (110), is tabulated, with four aging states: as-cast, 723 K, 773 K, 823 K. For 0.02Nb the values are Θ = 21.960/21.970/22.453/21.983, β = 0.424/0.462/0.428/0.457, βcosθ = 0.393/0.428/0.395/0.424, 4sinθ = 1.496/1.497/1.528/1.497. For 0.04Nb they are Θ = 21.937/22.014/22.073/21.980, β = 0.403/0.434/0.418/0.430, βcosθ = 0.373/0.402/0.387/0.398, 4sinθ = 1.494/1.499/1.503/1.497. The 773 K condition of 0.02Nb is an outlier with the largest Θ (22.453), largest 4sinθ (1.528) and smallest β (0.428). The table supplies the Williamson-Hall-type inputs (βcosθ versus 4sinθ) from which the citing text derives ferrite dislocation density and dislocation strengthening for each aging state.

observations.observation: Table 7 tabulates only the (110) reflection of ferrite; no other peaks are listed.
The table compares two steels, labelled '0.02Nb' and '0.04Nb', across four aging states: as-cast, 723 K, 773 K and 823 K.
For 0.02Nb, as-cast values are Θ = 21.960, β = 0.424, βcosθ = 0.393, 4sinθ = 1.496.
For 0.02Nb, the 773 K state is the maximum for Θ (22.453) and 4sinθ (1.528) and the minimum for β (0.428) among the four aging states.
For 0.04Nb, Θ ranges only from 21.937 (as-cast) to 22.073 (773 K), a much narrower spread than the 21.960-22.453 range of 0.02Nb.
In the as-cast state, 0.02Nb shows higher Θ (21.960 vs 21.937), β (0.424 vs 0.403), βcosθ (0.393 vs 0.373) and 4sinθ (1.496 vs 1.494) than 0.04Nb.
No units are printed for Θ, β, βcosθ or 4sinθ in the table header.
The caption states the table gives the values of θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ for ferrite in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.
The citing text states these θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ values are used (via a Williamson-Hall-type equation) to estimate dislocation density and dislocation strengthening in ferrite.
The citing text reports that dislocation strengthening of ferrite in the 0.02Nb steel is 79.7 MPa as-cast and 84.0, 83.5 and 93.3 MPa after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K respectively.

The citing text reports dislocation strengthening of ferrite in the 0.04Nb steel of 84.3 MPa as-cast and 92.2 and 96.4 MPa after aging at 723 and 773 K (the 823 K value is truncated in the supplied text).
The citing text specifies the calculation constants used with these values: Taylor factor M_F = 2, α_F = 0.4 and shear modulus G_F = 76 GPa for ferrite.
